policy.py is written at `/Users/Shared/rhythmbot_cap/fable-feedback/policy.py`. I could not execute it in this session (no shell tool), so it is verified by inspection only; the first feedback run will surface any runtime issue.

**Strategy summary**

- **Two independent fingertips sharing one gripper.** The hand is modelled as an L (−x) and an R (+x) tip. Each tick, per-tip (x, z) targets are merged into one keyframe: ref is the −x tip, width comes from the 3-D tip distance, and rise is the height difference. Constraints enforced are the tip-gap range (23 to 130 mm) and a roll limit of about 20 degrees.
- **Greedy note-to-finger assignment with feasibility checks.** Every note that becomes visible is assigned to a tip as a touch segment, or skipped. A candidate is accepted only if that tip has time to lift, travel at 0.9 m/s and descend between neighbouring touches, and if the other tip's overlapping touches are compatible: correct side, within max gap, and at least 35 mm apart when one tip must stay lifted while the other presses. Skipped notes are retried every tick in case the situation changes (for example a hold's end becoming known).
- **Chords** are tried as an L/R pair first, then individually. Small lateral offsets inside the half-lane tolerance (up to 19 mm) make tight pairs feasible, such as a tap next to a held lane or a 3-lane chord.
- **Finger choice** minimises travel, and for holds and slides prefers the tip whose free partner can reach the taps that fall during the long note. Taps get a small bias toward the tip whose partner can take the next note.
- **Trajectory generation.** Touch segments pin the tip at touch_z on the lane, with slides tracked through lane_at_offset using a 40 ms look-ahead. Between touches the tip follows a lift/travel/descend hop whose height adapts to the available time, so fast streams use low hops. A free tip rides inside the band permitted by the busy tip and is kept at least 10 mm above the screen whenever it has a touch within 0.3 s, so its next tap is a fresh touch. Taps stay pressed 80 ms past the hit to absorb arm lag.

**Next step** is to read feedback.md after the first run and tune the timing constants (lead, dwell, minimum hop time, roll limit) against what the judge reports.

policy.py is revised. I could not execute it here (no shell), so verification is by inspection again.

**What the feedback showed.** All six misses were notes my scheduler marked skipped, not execution failures. Hits were consistently early by about 20 ms with low spread, and every hold and slide kept 100% contact. The skips came from two weaknesses:

- **No lookahead in finger choice.** Notes were assigned to a fingertip the moment they appeared, 1.6 s ahead, before the following notes were visible. So a lane-4 tap took the left tip, and the lane-1 tap 0.28 s later was unreachable by the right tip and too far for the left one.
- **Feasibility demanded an on-time start.** The judge accepts touches up to 140 ms late, but I rejected any touch that could not begin exactly at the hit time.

**What changed**

- **Beam search instead of greedy assignment.** Every tick, all visible notes whose touch starts more than 0.25 s away are re-assigned by a beam search over (left, right, skip) choices in hit order, maximising completed notes and using travel cost as a tie-break. Notes about to start keep their assignment, and a small hysteresis term prevents flip-flopping. Chords are expanded as a left/right pair plus the single-note fallbacks.
- **Late starts within the window.** A touch may now begin up to 70 ms late if the fingertip's previous touch forces it. For holds and slides the allowance is capped at 12% of the duration so the 80% contact requirement still holds. Lateness carries a small cost so on-time choices win when available.
- **Tighter cycle.** Tap dwell dropped from 80 to 50 ms and the minimum lift-plus-descend time from 120 to 110 ms, since the observed arm lag is small. Planning speed is 1.0 m/s.
- **Orientation prior.** Long notes on the left half of the screen prefer the left tip and vice versa, so the free tip faces the rest of the screen. This addresses the skipped slide after a 5 s hold whose finger choice had been made with no information about later notes.

**Next step** is to check the new feedback for any late or lost-contact judgments, which would indicate the late-start allowance or shorter dwell is too aggressive.

policy.py is revised. Same caveat as before: no shell here, so the changes are checked by inspection only.

**What the feedback showed.** Both remaining misses were attempted this time but no touch registered, and both share a pattern: a long sideways move right after a tap (2 lanes in 0.25 s, 4 lanes in 0.31 s). My hop let the x command finish only about 0.1 s before the commanded touchdown, and in the previous run the hit timing spread was widest on exactly these charts. The arm lags fast lateral commands, so the tip most likely touched while still short of the target lane, outside the half-lane tolerance.

**What changed**

- **x arrives early and faster.** The hop now moves the x command at up to 1.2 m/s and aims to have it in place 120 ms before touchdown, instead of letting travel overlap the end of the descent. Far-off notes still get a slow, smooth move since the arrival deadline, not the speed cap, sets the pace.
- **Settle time in the feasibility test.** The time a fingertip needs between touches is now the larger of the lift-plus-descend minimum and travel distance at 0.9 m/s plus a 120 ms settle. When that forces a late start, the touch is scheduled late rather than rejected.
- **Slightly more late allowance and shorter dwell.** Taps may start up to 90 ms late (contact lands ~20 ms before the command, so this stays inside the 140 ms window), and the tap dwell dropped from 50 to 40 ms. Together these buy the ~30 ms that the two failed moves were short by.

**What to watch in the next feedback:** any "late" or out-of-lane judgments would mean the lag is larger than assumed and the settle time should grow further, trading a few impossible notes for reliability on the rest.

policy.py is revised; as before, verified by inspection only since there is no shell in this session.

**What the feedback showed.** The same two taps failed, both a long sideways move straight after another tap (2 lanes in 0.25 s and 4 lanes in 0.31 s), and the judge saw no fresh touch in the lane. Every other note is at perfect level, so the bottleneck is purely how quickly a fingertip can be settled in a distant lane after a touch.

**What changed**

- **Drag away during the tap dwell.** Once a tap has registered, a pressed tip cannot trigger anything else, so it may start sliding toward its next lane 15 ms after the touch instead of waiting for the dwell and lift. The touch piece of the trajectory now carries a drag target, and the feasibility test counts travel from that moment. This buys about 40 ms on every tap-to-tap move for free.
- **Settle time scales with the move.** The lag error of the arm grows with how far it just moved, so the x command must now arrive 100 ms plus 0.4 s per metre before touchdown, rather than a flat 120 ms. A 2-lane move gets 140 ms, a 4-lane move 180 ms.
- **Faster x command, slightly more late allowance.** The x command moves at up to 1.4 m/s, and taps may start up to 110 ms late. With hits landing about 20 ms before the commanded touchdown, that still sits inside the 140 ms window.

For the two training misses this means the 2-lane case is now scheduled with roughly 0.19 s of settling before touchdown, and the 4-lane case is attempted at the edge of the window. Both were attempted before without harming the following notes, so the downside on unseen charts is small.

policy.py is revised. No shell here, so verified by inspection.

**What the feedback showed.** The same two taps failed for the third run, both a 2-to-4 lane move directly after a tap, and both reported as "no fresh touch in its lane" while the very next note in the same lane succeeded. The consistent picture is that the arm's lateral motion lags more than my model assumed for big moves: the tip comes down while still short of the lane, then slides into it already pressed, which the judge correctly ignores as not fresh. The one earlier case of a 3-lane move that did succeed was judged "great", also pointing at lateral lag of several tens of milliseconds.

**What changed**

- **Longer settle for long moves.** The x command must now arrive 100 ms plus 0.8 s per metre before touchdown (was 0.4 s per metre). For a 2-lane move the commanded touchdown lands about 55 ms after the hit, well inside the 140 ms window, instead of 25 ms. A 4-lane move after a tap now exceeds the allowed lateness and is skipped, which costs nothing since it never succeeded.
- **Low hops.** Between touches the tip now rises to only 20 mm instead of using the full 35 mm hover, and idles there too. The final descent becomes about 130 ms, so the lateral motion is settled before the tip is anywhere near the screen, and the fresh-touch lift margin is still four times the contact threshold.

**What to watch:** if the next feedback shows the 2-lane case as a late or out-of-lane touch again, the arm's lateral speed is lower than the 0.9 m/s the API suggests, and I would lower the planning speed itself rather than add more settle time.

policy.py is revised; verified by inspection (no shell in this session).

**What the feedback showed.** The 2-lane move that failed three times now succeeds, but two notes that had passed in every earlier run failed, and hit timing on four charts is now so consistent (spread of 2 to 4 ms) that any late-scheduled touch stands out as the failure. Both regressions had their touchdown pushed later by last round's settle rule, and that later touchdown landed inside the window where the *other* fingertip starts preparing for its own next touch: it lifts to the fresh height and the gap widens, which rolls the hand by up to 20 degrees exactly as the busy tip lands. For the failed slide there was a second problem: a late touch was aimed at where the slide had already moved, not the start lane the judge checks.

**What changed**

- **The free tip is always lifted, with a gentle constant roll.** Whenever one tip is committed to a touch, the other now rides 12 mm above it with the gap opened to at least 50 mm (about 14 degrees of roll), rather than lying on the screen and lurching up only when its own touch is near. This removes both the sudden roll at touchdown and any chance of stray contact by the idle tip.
- **Pre-roll while both tips hover.** When one tip's touch is within 0.25 s and the other's is not, the other is lifted and the gap opened already, so the configuration is set before the descent starts and nothing moves at the moment of contact. Chords, where both descend together, are excluded.
- **Late slide touches aim at the start lane.** A slide whose touch is delayed now targets the lane at its hit time and catches up with the moving target over the next 150 ms, instead of landing where the path has moved to.

The remaining skip is a 4-lane move after a chord. It has never succeeded in any run, and the search already trades it for a reachable note, so nothing is lost there.

policy.py is revised; verified by inspection (no shell in this session).

**What the feedback showed.** Across all six revisions the picture is consistent. On every chart where all notes succeed, hit timing is clustered within 2 ms, and the two remaining failures are exactly the notes my scheduler planned with a deliberately late touchdown (55 to 70 ms after the hit). No touch planned more than about 20 ms late has clearly registered in any run, no matter how I tuned lateral settle. The most plausible cause is on my side: a note appears to leave the perception list at its hit time, and my code then froze its segment and lifted the finger mid-descent, so the late touch was never actually made.

**What changed**

- **Finish touches for notes that vanish just before touchdown.** If a note disappears while its touch is within 150 ms of starting, the segment is kept as a ghost and the touch is completed, rather than aborted. If the note reappears in perception, it resumes as a normal assignment. For long notes the ghost is capped at 250 ms.
- **Late plans are now worth less in the search.** A touch scheduled late counts as a fraction of a note in the beam's objective, falling to 0.5 at 100 ms late but never below a skip. The search now prefers plans that reach a note on time with the other, already hovering fingertip over same-finger sprints that arrive late. In both failing cases such an on-time plan exists.
- **Settle rule relaxed.** Settle after a move is back to 100 ms plus 0.6 s per metre, since the previous 0.8 s per metre was manufacturing late plans that then failed.

Both changes are general: dense unseen charts will produce many near-infeasible moves, and the policy now resolves them by finger choice first and by late touches only as a last resort.

policy.py is revised; verified by inspection (no shell in this session).

**What the feedback showed.** The two long-move notes that had failed in every earlier run now succeed, confirming last round's diagnosis. One new failure appeared: slide #19 in varied-103, which starts 0.25 s after the previous slide ends in the same lane and had passed in all six earlier runs. What changed for it is the role swap: with the previous slide now played on time by the other tip, the tip that just released has to become the lifted one. My pre-roll logic commanded that tip to rise 34 mm and open the gap by up to 100 mm within a single tick, right as the other tip was descending onto the lane. That kind of step swings the whole gripper at the worst moment.

**What changed**

- **Pre-roll eases in.** The lifted tip's rise and the gap opening now ramp over 120 ms as the other tip's touch approaches, finishing just as the descent starts, instead of stepping to their final values at once.
- **Free tips are rate-limited vertically as well as laterally.** A free tip may now move at most 0.5 m/s vertically and 1.2 m/s laterally between keyframes, so re-planning or role swaps never produce a jump.
- **Roll limit enforced at every keyframe.** After rate limiting, if the height difference would exceed the roll limit for the current gap, the free tip waits for the gap to open rather than rolling the hand past 20 degrees. Previously the limit was only guaranteed at the target configuration, not during transitions.

The one remaining skip is the 4-lane move after a chord, where the search trades it for the reachable note that follows, which is the right call.
